name: On-site storm-water retention, infiltration and reuse with geocellular tanks (ACO StormBrixx), as proposed by STC
owner: ACO (manufacturer, plastic geocellular tanks); proposed for Tunisia by STC, its exclusive Tunisian distributor

claims.claim: StormBrixx SD is a patented plastic geocellular system for storm-water attenuation and infiltration with a 97% void ratio
A 2,000 m2 asphalt site needs about 90 m3 of storage (2,000 x 0.9 x 0.05 m), so about 93 m3 of StormBrixx SD
The stored water can feed garden irrigation in summer (pump outside STC's range)
On sandy soil an unlined tank allows infiltration and groundwater recharge
Most Tunisian cities have no separate storm-water network, so rain and sewage share the same pipes
Tunisian rules require rainwater collection tanks in new buildings and encourage alternative storm-water techniques

greenwashingFlags: self-certified: 97% void ratio, 50/60-year design life and 'recyclable' come from the manufacturer's own datasheet (SRC-TG-641)
unverifiable claim: water-supply benefit is stated with assumed values and no measured Tunisian case (SRC-TG-341)

impact shifted elsewhere: the product is a flood-attenuation tool presented here as a water-supply and recharge answer; no source gives a yield, and the infiltration option moves road and roof pollutants towards groundwater (SRC-TG-643)
limits: Yield is bounded by rainfall: about 600, 300 and 150 mm a year in the north, centre and south (SRC-TG-642). Most of it falls in a few intense events and long droughts recur, so a tank sized for one big storm stays empty for most of the year and overflows in the biggest events.

Stored water is not drinking water. It can serve only non-potable uses, with a separate network and yearly laboratory control for roof water (SRC-TG-640, pp. 17-18). Run-off from asphalt is dirtier than roof water.
Storage only makes sense if the water is then used (SRC-TG-640, p. 36). In winter, when the tank fills, irrigation demand is low; summer demand has to be met from water stored for months.

Infiltration depends on soil and on the water being clean. Metals and hydrocarbons accumulate in infiltration systems and travel from 5-10 cm to over 1 m depending on the device (SRC-TG-643, abstract). Which Tunisian soils and aquifers are suitable is not documented in what we opened.

blockers.blocker: Decree 2018-171, Article 8, as summarised by ANME, covers use of water from inaccessible building roofs. We found no text covering reuse of run-off from asphalt or car parks, which is the vendor's example. The decree text was not opened.
Water is cheap: ANME puts an annual household bill at about 64 TND and calls rainwater collection 'economiquement non rentable', so private users have little reason to pay for storage.

On-site infiltration and retention are recommendations to municipalities (urban plans, building permits), not obligations. Stormwater networks sit with communes, and flood-protection works are excluded from their duty.
No Tunisian price, installer base or design standard for geocellular tanks was found; the datasheet is a New Zealand version.
The pump for reuse is outside STC's product range, so the supply use is incomplete as proposed.

criticisms.criticism: The proposal is a vendor's: written by an STC employee to match STC products to Tunisian problems, with assumed values, press-sourced problem figures and no measured saving or installed case.
criticisms.from: our own review of SRC-TG-341 (STC is the exclusive distributor of ACO)

criticisms.criticism: Stored storm water is not a water source: storing it only makes sense if it is then used, and the incentive for private users is too weak.
criticisms.from: ANME guide (Tunisian national agency, guide to municipalities)

criticisms.criticism: Infiltrating urban run-off can carry metals and hydrocarbons into soil and potentially groundwater; results are mixed and site-dependent.
criticisms.from: Tedoldi et al. 2016 (peer-reviewed review, mostly temperate-climate sites)

criticisms.criticism: Rainwater, even from roofs, is often contaminated; chlorination does not remove heavy metals, and owners seldom test it.

tradeOffs.effect: Runs against the cheaper traditional option: the majel (underground cistern) costs 13,000-15,000 TND for 20 m3 in masonry and under 4,000 TND in plastic (about 650-750 and under 200 TND per m3 of storage, our calculation). No StormBrixx price was found, so no like-for-like comparison is possible.
Infiltration may add urban pollutants to soil and groundwater. This is a risk shown for soil-based systems elsewhere, not measured in Tunisia.

Plastic (polypropylene) tanks bury a material with a stated 50-60 year life; end-of-life handling and the recycled share are not documented. Electricity for the reuse pump adds a small energy load, not quantified.
Climate trend: rainfall is projected to fall by 6-9% by 2050 (AFD) or more, with more extreme events (NDC), which favours flood attenuation over supply.

gapLeft: Both targets, regional supply capacity and network losses behind the 2023 rationing (FND-TG-451) and the groundwater overdraft of 865 Mm3 a year (FND-TG-410), stay untouched. Urban flooding itself, the problem this product best fits, has no finding yet.
conflictOfInterest: Proposed by expert EXP-TG-001 (Maher Mahmoudi), a Technical Sales Engineer at STC, the exclusive Tunisian distributor of ACO (SRC-TG-341). STC would profit from sales of StormBrixx. His proposal is treated as vendor material (tier C); the checks below use sources that do not come from STC or ACO, apart from the manufacturer datasheet used for product specifications only.
author: TahaGHZ
outstanding: open the text of Decree 2018-171 (Articles 3, 6, 7, 8, 9) and Decree 2016-1125 and check how ANME paraphrases them, including whether run-off from paved areas is covered; find a StormBrixx or equivalent price in Tunisia and a cost per m3 stored for open basins and SuDS; find Tunisian rain-event statistics (events per year, intensity) and soil infiltration suitability; open the full text of Tedoldi et al. 2016; check the AllAfrica claim on combined sewers and the ONAS rule on storm water in sewers; confirm the ACO datasheet table values from an official ACO page; ask EXP-TG-001 for any Tunisian installed case.
excerpt: ACO StormBrixx is a patented, injection-moulded polypropylene crate system that is buried to form a tank holding 95-97% water by volume. It is used to hold run-off from roofs and paved areas and release it slowly…

sections.heading: What it is
sections.content:
ACO StormBrixx is a patented, injection-moulded polypropylene crate system that is buried to form a tank holding 95-97% water by volume. It is used to hold run-off from roofs and paved areas and release it slowly (attenuation), to let it soak into the ground (infiltration), or to store it for reuse (SRC-TG-641). STC proposes it for Tunisian sites in "Scenario B" of its use-case paper: a worked example holds the run-off of 2,000 m2 of asphalt in about 93 m3 of tanks, with summer irrigation through a pump, or an unlined tank for infiltration on sandy soil (SRC-TG-341). The paper is confidential and must not be published without EXP-TG-001's agreement.

Status in Tunisia: proposed. SRC-TG-341 gives no installed case and we found none.

sections.heading: What it claims, and what the evidence shows
sections.content:
- **Product specification (97% void ratio, patented, polypropylene).** Repeated in the manufacturer's New Zealand datasheet (SRC-TG-641). That is the same owner, so it is the claim restated, not verification. Partial.
- **The 90 m3 / 93 m3 example.** The arithmetic holds (2,000 x 0.9 x 0.05 = 90 m3; 90 / 0.97 = about 93 m3), but the 50 mm design storm is assumed. The ANME guide suggests holding 5 to 15 mm per m2 on a plot (SRC-TG-640, p. 36). A 50 mm storm is a large event; the guide does not call for it. Partial.
- **Annual water captured.** The vendor gives no annual figure. As an upper bound, our calculation, 2,000 m2 x 0.9 runoff factor on the FAO regional rainfall of 600, 300 and 150 mm (SRC-TG-642) gives at most about 1,080, 540 and 270 m3 a year (north, centre, south). This is before first-flush loss, overflow when the tank is full and losses in use. The real figure depends on the number and size of events, which no source we opened gives. Evaporation from a buried tank is small, but stored water can degrade, as the ANME guide describes for cisterns (SRC-TG-640, pp. 10, 17-18). Evidence: none for the supply claim; not verified.
- **Scale against our findings.** To offset the 865 Mm3 groundwater overdraft in 2020 (SRC-TG-503, via FND-TG-410) at the northern maximum above, about 800,000 such sites would be needed (our calculation). The overdraft is not caused by lack of storage but by withdrawals above renewable supply (FND-TG-410).
- **Infiltration and recharge.** The review of infiltration systems finds metals and hydrocarbons accumulate in the soil, mostly in the top 10-30 cm, with contrary cases (SRC-TG-643). A buried tank discharges below that top layer, so the filtering role of the surface soil is lost; this is our inference, not tested in the review. Partial.
- **No separate storm-water network.** SRC-TG-341 attributes this to a press article (AllAfrica), not opened. ANME says communes lack equipment against flood risk and that interventions do not solve flooding (SRC-TG-640, p. 13). Not verified as stated.

sections.heading: Audit
sections.content:
**root_cause_coverage: 1.** FND-TG-451 lists regional supply capacity, project delays, drought and network efficiency as causes; FND-TG-410 lists withdrawals above renewable recharge, illicit drilling and free drilling. Site-scale storage touches none of these. It could marginally reduce the draw of one site on SONEDE water for irrigation and, if infiltrated and clean, add a little local recharge. Its natural target, run-off and flooding, is outside our findings.

**evidence_quality: 1.** The only sources on the product are the manufacturer's datasheet and an STC employee's paper with assumed values. Independent evidence exists only for general principles (ANME on cisterns and retention; Tedoldi on infiltration). No measured Tunisian result.

**adoption: 0.** Status is proposed; we found no installation in Tunisia and no price list. Majels, by contrast, are widespread (about 150,000 in Sfax, SRC-TG-640, p. 10), so the user need exists but is served by a different technology.

**side_effects: 2.** No documented harm; the main risk is pollutant transfer to groundwater when infiltration is used, and plastic end-of-life. Both are risks, not observations in Tunisia.

**cost_accessibility: 1.** No StormBrixx price was found, so cost per m3 cannot be given. The comparison point is the plastic majel cistern at under 200 TND per m3 of storage (our calculation from SRC-TG-640, p. 15). Tank, excavation, geotextile, pump and yearly lab tests for roof water add to cost; with low water tariffs ANME judges collection unprofitable. Score is low-confidence.

sections.heading: Limits and blockers
sections.content:
- **Climate.** Tunisian rain is concentrated in few events, with long droughts (SRC-TG-640, p. 6; SRC-TG-642). Storage sized for flood peaks serves supply poorly. Rainfall is expected to fall by 6-9% by 2050 (SRC-TG-504) or 10-30% (SRC-TG-508, source unspecified) while extreme events become more frequent, which favours the flood-protection use.
- **Law.** Decree 2018-171 (19 February 2018), as summarised in SRC-TG-640 (pp. 17-19): Article 3 requires new civil buildings and larger projects to include a rainwater tank backed by a feasibility study approved by the agriculture ministry; Article 8 allows roof water for non-drinking uses through a separate network; Article 9 requires annual laboratory tests. So Tunisian law already requires roof-water tanks in new buildings, which makes the product a possible way to comply, but nothing we found names geocellular tanks or covers run-off from asphalt. Infiltration is only recommended (SRC-TG-640, p. 39). **The decree text was not opened.**
- **Institutions.** Communes manage storm-water networks (Code des collectivités locales, Article 240) except flood-protection works (SRC-TG-640, p. 14). A parcel-scale product needs municipal rules to create demand.
- **Technical.** Soil type, depth to groundwater and pollutant load decide whether infiltration is safe; the vendor gives none of these for Tunisia.

sections.heading: Criticisms
sections.content: See `criticisms` in the frontmatter. The two best-supported are that the proposal is vendor-authored with assumed values (supported) and that stored run-off is only worth it if reused, which private users have little incentive to do (supported by ANME). The pollutant criticism is general: it comes from a review of temperate sites and says infiltration often retains pollutants in the top soil, so it is partly supported for Tunisia.

sections.heading: Trade-offs and consequences
sections.content:
- **Water:** possible groundwater-quality risk if untreated run-off is infiltrated (long-term, a risk argued from SRC-TG-643, not seen in Tunisia).
- **Agriculture:** small irrigation reuse for gardens; no effect on irrigated agriculture, the main groundwater user (FND-TG-410).
- **Energy:** a reuse pump adds electricity use; not quantified.
- **Materials:** polypropylene tank with stated 50-60 year life; end-of-life not documented.
- **Urban flooding is not in our findings.** This product probably matters most for run-off and flood attenuation, a problem our phase 1 does not cover (ANME describes floods in several cities, SRC-TG-640, p. 6). It is a gap for phase 1 to research. Nothing here is linked under `creates`.

sections.heading: Verdict and gap
sections.content: **superficial** for the targets we have. It does not act on the root causes of FND-TG-451 or FND-TG-410, and the supply benefit is unquantified. This is not a failed product: as flood attenuation it may be sound, but no finding covers that problem and no source we opened tests it in Tunisia. For phase 3: compare on-site tanks with majels and open basins (cost per m3 stored and per m3 used), test the roof-water route that Decree 2018-171 already mandates, and combine retention with managed aquifer recharge only where soils and run-off quality are checked. Phase 1 should add a finding on urban flooding and storm-water losses.

sections.heading: Verification
sections.content: **Outstanding verification:** open the text of Decree 2018-171 (Articles 3, 6, 7, 8, 9) and Decree 2016-1125 and check how ANME paraphrases them, including whether run-off from paved areas is covered; find a StormBrixx or equivalent price in Tunisia and a cost per m3 stored for open basins and SuDS; find Tunisian rain-event statistics (events per year, intensity) and soil infiltration suitability; open the full text of Tedoldi et al. 2016; check the AllAfrica claim on combined sewers and the ONAS rule on storm water in sewers; confirm the ACO datasheet table values from an official ACO page; ask EXP-TG-001 for any Tunisian installed case.

targetItems.title: Supply cuts went from "very rare" in 2009 to national rationing in 2023-2024, and they persist where regional transfer and network capacity lag, even when national dam stocks recover
Even the national water strategy's own target scenario keeps aquifers overdrawn until the 2040s, and an earlier projection of the groundwater resource fell below later resource estimates

resolvedSources.title: Elaboration de la vision et de la stratégie du secteur de l'eau à l'horizon 2050 pour la Tunisie « EAU 2050 » – Synthèse de l'étude
resolvedSources.publisher: Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Ressources Hydrauliques et de la Pêche Maritime (MARHP), Bureau de la Planification et des Equilibres Hydrauliques; study by STUDI International / GKW
resolvedSources.extracts:
Section III, printed page 3 (PDF page 4):

> C'est ainsi que grâce au MHE il a été possible d'établir, dès l'Etape Diagnostic un résultat décisif, celui du risque certain d'un « crash hydrique » dès 2030, c'est-à-dire une rupture systémique entre l'offre et la demande d'eau en Tunisie dès cet horizon, somme toute trop proche, avec les graves conséquences encourues.

English gloss: Using the hydro-economic model (MHE), the diagnostic stage established the "certain risk" of a "water crash" from 2030, meaning a systemic break between water supply and demand in Tunisia by that horizon.

Section I, printed page 1 (PDF page 2) (legacy factors):

> i. Les usagers, qu'ils relèvent du champ du domestique, de l'agricole, des industries et services ou de l'urbain, ont été habitués à une perception d'« abondance », puisqu'ils « n'ont jamais manqué d'eau » pendant les longues décennies passées ;
> ii. En plus, l'approvisionnement des usagers s'est toujours passé avec des tarifs subventionnés et entièrement déconnecté des coûts ;
> iii. L'attention des acteurs étaient plus focalisée sur les eaux de surface que les eaux souterraines, d'où a résulté, en termes d'aménagement, un beaucoup plus grand centrage sur les barrages et retenues d'eau que sur les aquifères ;
> iv. Le caractère globalement aride du pays n'était pas suffisamment pris en compte

English gloss: (i) Users in every sector were used to a perception of "abundance", having "never lacked water" for decades. (ii) Supply has always been at subsidised tariffs, entirely disconnected from costs. (iii) Planners focused on surface water, dams and reservoirs more than on aquifers. (iv) The country's overall aridity was not sufficiently taken into account.

Section 8 "Conditions de Financement", printed page 12 (PDF page 13):

> L'investissement annuel moyen additionnel d'Eau 2050, en dehors de l'« engagé », est de 2,6 MDS, alors que la moyenne annuelle des Investissements de l'Etat (Titre II) pour les années 2019 à 2022 est de 4,1 MDS. Ainsi, sur la base de l'existant, ce qui est envisagé pour le Plan d'action Eau 2050 correspond à 63% de l'ensemble du Titre II, ce qui est inenvisageable.

English gloss: The additional average annual investment of Eau 2050 is 2.6 billion dinars, against an average state capital budget (Titre II) of 4.1 billion dinars in 2019-2022. The plan would equal 63% of the whole Titre II, which is "unthinkable".

Section I, printed page 2 (PDF page 3):

> vi. L'agriculture irriguée, qui utilise 80% des ressources, est loin de fonctionner à l'optimum

English gloss: Irrigated agriculture, which uses 80% of resources, is far from operating at its optimum.

Section V, printed page 6 (PDF page 7):

> Le tableau suivant donne un bilan offre-demande jusqu'à l'horizon de l'étude (2050) ; un équilibre hydrique est atteint.

English gloss: The following table gives a supply-demand balance to the study horizon (2050); a water balance is reached.

Table "BILAN RESSOURCE - DEMANDE EN EAU - SCENARIO EAU ET DEVELOPPEMENT DURABLE - À L'HORIZON 2050", printed page 7 (PDF page 8). Rows as extracted with `pdftotext -raw` (columns 2020 / 2025 / 2030 / 2035 / 2040 / 2050):

> Projections démographiques (106 Hab.) 11,9 12,4 12,9 13,1 13,4 13,8
> Scénario climatique à l'horizon 2050 (2041-2063) - - - - RCP4.5 RCP4.5
> Apport potentiel (moyen) 2732 2732 2732 2732 2186 2186
> Apport en année vingtennale sèche (garanti 19 années sur 20) 851 851 851 851 510 510
> Ressources en eaux souterraines renouvelables 2190 2190 2190 2190 2190 2190
> Total ressources conventionnelles (Mm3) 4922 4922 5147 5147 4601 4601
> Réutilisation des eaux épurées 59 106 143 196 304 485
> Dessalement de l'eau de mer 18 91 192 265 265 265
> Total ressources conventionnelles et non conventionnelles 4999 5119 5482 5607 5170 5350
> Disponibilité m3/an/hab. 422 411 426 427 386 387
> Demande en eau potable (AEP) 780 839 880 930 990 1100
> Demande en eau d'irrigation stabilisée (climato-économique) 3382 3132 3175 3082 2653 2502
> Balance surexploitation / sous exploitation des nappes -865 -567 -334 -186 -142 28
> Taux d'exploitation des nappes (%) 139% 126% 115% 108% 106% 99%

English gloss: Supply-demand balance under the strategy's "Water and Sustainable Development" scenario. Population rises from 11.9 million (2020) to 13.8 million (2050). From 2040 the climate scenario is RCP4.5 (period 2041-2063). Mean surface inflow ("apport potentiel moyen") falls from 2,732 to 2,186 Mm3. The 1-in-20 dry-year inflow falls from 851 to 510 Mm3. Total conventional resources go from 4,922 to 4,601 Mm3. Availability per inhabitant, counting desalination and treated wastewater, goes from 422 m3/yr (2020) to 387 m3/yr (2050). Aquifer exploitation rate falls from 139% (2020) to 99% (2050), and the irrigation demand is assumed to fall from 3,382 to 2,502 Mm3.
resolvedSources.notes:
- Opened via: curl+pdftotext (layout, plus `-raw` for the table page); saw: full text (synthesis, about 10 pages).
- The document is undated. It costs its action plan in "Millions de Dinars constants '2023'", so it was finalised in 2023 or later. The study was launched in 2019.
- The table is a normative scenario: the 2050 balance assumes the strategy is fully executed (irrigation demand cut by about 26%, more reuse and desalination, aquifers brought back to balance). It is not a no-action projection.
- Per-capita availability here includes non-conventional water, so it is not comparable with "renewable resources per capita" figures from other sources.
- The pdftotext `-layout` output scrambled the table. The `-raw` output gave coherent rows, which were checked arithmetically: 4922+77 = 4999, and 4601+749 = 5350.

resolvedSources.extracts:
Executive summary, printed page 10 (precipitation):

> une diminution des précipitations annuelles (entre -6% et -9% en 2050 et entre -9% et -18% en 2100 par rapport à la période de référence 1981-2010) sont attendues sous changement climatique

English gloss: Annual precipitation is expected to fall by 6-9% by 2050 and by 9-18% by 2100, relative to the 1981-2010 reference.

Executive summary, printed pages 10-11 (runoff, per capita):

> montrent une nette diminution des apports en eau qui varie selon les scénarios de 25 à 36% à l'horizon 2050 et de 33 à 61% à l'horizon 2100. En considérant uniquement l'élévation de température et en prenant une pluviométrie constante jusqu'à 2100, les écoulements baissent de 7 à 11% en 2050 et de 9 à 20% en 2100 selon les différentes formules. Nous constatons que le tiers de la diminution des écoulements est dû à l'augmentation de l'évapotranspiration et les 2/3 reviennent à la diminution de la quantité de pluie.

> Le quota en ressources renouvelables par habitant et par an pourrait passer de 366 m3 actuellement à 200 m3 en 2050 et moins de 150 m3 en 2100.

English gloss: Inflows fall by 25-36% by 2050 and by 33-61% by 2100, depending on scenario. With rainfall held constant (warming only), runoff falls by 7-11% by 2050. One third of the decline comes from higher evapotranspiration and two thirds from less rain. Renewable resources per inhabitant would go from 366 m3/yr now to 200 m3 in 2050 and below 150 m3 in 2100.

Section 2.2, printed page 40 (historical baseline):

> Durant les 3 dernières décennies (90/91-2015/2016), on a enregistré 11 années hydrologiquement sèches pour uniquement 6 années humides. L'apport moyen en eau de surface pour la période est de l'ordre de 2700 millions de m3.

English gloss: Over 1990/91-2015/16 there were 11 hydrologically dry years against 6 wet ones. Mean surface inflow for the period was about 2,700 Mm3.

Table 6, printed page 42, as extracted with `pdftotext -raw`. Columns: reference period, RCP4.5 2050, RCP4.5 2100, RCP8.5 2050, RCP8.5 2100, official MARHP value.

> National Apports 2494 1645 1577 1762 1025 2700
> Variation en % -34% -37% -29% -59%

English gloss: National surface inflow is 2,494 Mm3 in the modelled reference period. It falls to 1,645 (-34%) under RCP4.5 by 2050 and to 1,762 (-29%) under RCP8.5 by 2050. By 2100 it falls to 1,577 (RCP4.5) and 1,025 (RCP8.5). The official MARHP value is 2,700 Mm3.

Printed page 42, below Table 6:

> Une étude récente13 montre que les évènements extrêmes de précipitations pourraient être moins fréquents et moins intenses au Sud de la Méditerranée qu'au Nord sous l'effet du changement climatique. L'idée selon laquelle, des précipitations extrêmes plus fréquentes et plus copieuses pourraient être suffisantes en 2050 pour recharger les ouvrages et les nappes apparaît donc comme une hypothèse particulièrement optimiste.

English gloss: Extreme rainfall may become less frequent and less intense south of the Mediterranean. The idea that bigger storms will refill dams and aquifers by 2050 is therefore "particularly optimistic".

Printed page 42 (agriculture's share of resources):

> Une nouvelle approche de l'allocation des ressources devient inéluctable et aura un impact très important sur les différents secteurs et surtout le secteur agricole qui exploite plus de 80% des ressources.

English gloss: A new approach to allocating water becomes unavoidable and will hit agriculture hardest, since it uses more than 80% of resources.

Printed page 43 (groundwater, coastal aquifers):

> Les eaux souterraines renouvelables pourraient passer de 1524 millions de m3 actuellement à pratiquement 1000 millions de m3 en 2050 et 700 millions en 2100, soit la moitié des ressources actuelles. Au niveau des nappes côtières les pertes seront plus importantes à la suite de l'élévation du niveau de la mer et pourraient atteindre 50% de leurs ressources en 2050 et beaucoup plus en 2100.

English gloss: Renewable groundwater would go from 1,524 Mm3 now to about 1,000 Mm3 in 2050 and 700 Mm3 in 2100. Losses in coastal aquifers will be larger because of sea-level rise and could reach 50% of their resources by 2050.

Table 8, printed page 43 (`-raw`). Columns: official MARHP value (Mm3), RCP4.5 2050, RCP4.5 2100, RCP8.5 2050, RCP8.5 2100.

> Total 1620 1069 1021 1150 664
> Variation en % -34% -37% -29% -59%

English gloss: Groundwater resources go from 1,620 Mm3 (official) to 1,069 (RCP4.5) or 1,150 (RCP8.5) Mm3 by 2050.

Section 2.2.4, printed page 44:

> Les nappes côtières qui connaissent une surexploitation subiront une accélération de l'intrusion marine sous l'effet de la remonté du niveau de la mer estimée entre 30 et 50 cm en 2050. Environ la moitié des réserves dans les nappes phréatiques littorales risquent de disparaitre.

English gloss: Overexploited coastal aquifers will see accelerated seawater intrusion as the sea rises by an estimated 30-50 cm by 2050. About half of the reserves in coastal shallow aquifers risk disappearing.

Executive summary, printed page 17 (demand):

> La demande totale en eau augmenterait autour de 38%. Cependant, les ressources risquent de baisser considérablement avec moins 28% en 2050 et moins 59% en 2100, creusant fortement le déficit hydrique.

English gloss: Total water demand would rise by about 38%, while resources may fall by 28% by 2050 and 59% by 2100.

Section 3.3.2, printed page 115:

> La demande en eau bleue a été estimée à 3,1 milliards de m3 en 2018. Elle est satisfaite par une exploitation intensive des eaux souterraines s'élevant à plus de 123% des ressources totales.

> Au cours de la troisième année de sècheresse 2015/2018, le quota alloué aux périmètres publics irrigués a été réduit à 27% par rapport à l'approvisionnement habituel27.

> En 2018, trois quarts des ressources exploitées sont consommées par le secteur agricole pour l'irrigation de 406 540 ha, soit un volume de 2,4 milliards de m3, dont 84% provient des eaux souterraines et seulement 16% des eaux des barrages.

English gloss: Blue-water demand was 3.1 billion m3 in 2018, met by groundwater exploitation above 123% of total resources. In the third drought year of 2015-2018, quotas for public irrigated schemes were cut to 27% of normal supply. In 2018, agriculture used three quarters of exploited resources, 2.4 billion m3 for 406,540 ha, 84% of it from groundwater.

Printed pages 115-116 (assumptions behind the balances; the 913 Mm3 sentence starts on page 115, the other sentences are on page 116):

> qui atteindrait 913 millions de M3 en 2050

> des ressources non conventionnelles mobilisables incluant REUT et dessalement, soit 626 millions de M3, ce qui représente dix les volumes actuels réutilisés et dessalés
> des économies d'eau de l'ordre de 900 millions de M3

> Les hypothèses ainsi retenues, permettent de montrer un bilan potentiellement excédentaire de 16% en 2050 sous réserve que soient assurés les investissements pour mobiliser les ressources non conventionnelles, éviter les pertes d'eau dans les réseaux et améliorer la collecte des eaux pluviales.

> les données STUDI-GKW ont été corrigées pour prendre en compte la hausse de l'évapotranspiration, qui augmente ,la demande de l'ordre de 4.6 % en 2050 et 9.1% en 2100

> l'importation nette d'eau virtuelle ­ estimée en 2013 à 4,7 milliards de m330, est en train de dépasser sensiblement le volume des ressources nationales.

English gloss: Drinking-water demand reaches 913 Mm3 in 2050 (STUDI-GKW). The Eau 2050 scenario adds 626 Mm3 of reuse and desalination (ten times current volumes) and about 900 Mm3 of savings. That gives a potential 16% surplus in 2050, provided the investments are made. Higher evapotranspiration raises irrigation demand by 4.6% (2050) and 9.1% (2100). Net virtual-water imports (4.7 billion m3 in 2013) are overtaking national resources.

> Les prévisions déjà publiées à l'horizon 2050 (ITES) se basent sur l'hypothèse d'une baisse maitrisée de la demande en eau agricole et sur une augmentation sensible de la demande en eau potable tous secteurs confondus (domestique, industriel, touristique) selon le MARHP dans la stratégie EAU2030, mais ne tient pas compte les effets du CC sur les ressources comme sur la demande.

resolvedSources.notes:
- Opened via: curl+pdftotext (layout, plus `-raw` for pages 42, 43 and 115); saw: full text, about 120 pages.
- Dated April 2021 ("Avril 2021 – Version finale"). The World Bank CCDR cites it as "Agence française de développement, 2020"; the tables say "Élaboration étude, 2020".
- Method: national 5 km climate model, 1981-2100, under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5. Runoff comes from empirical water-balance formulas (Tixeront, Turc, Schreiber), not a calibrated hydrological model. Groundwater recharge is assumed to change by the same rate as surface runoff, which is a strong simplification.
- Internal inconsistencies:
  - Renewable groundwater is 1,524 Mm3 in the text but 1,620 Mm3 in Table 8.
  - The 2100 range for the runoff decline is 33-61% in the summary but 31-61% in the body.
  - The modelled reference runoff (2,494 Mm3) is below the official MARHP 2,700 Mm3.
  - Page 40 gives blue-water potential of about 4.8 billion m3, or 436 m3 per inhabitant per year, while pages 11 and 43 give 366 m3 of renewable resources per inhabitant. The two figures use different numerators.
- Independence: the 2050 balances reuse STUDI-GKW (Eau 2050) resource and demand calculations (page 116), and the 2018 column is MARHP data. Agreement with SRC-TG-503 is therefore not independent confirmation.
- Verified by the source-verifier on 2026-11-21: the ONAGRI file was re-downloaded, and all extracts match the document at the pages given.
- Table 30 values come from the `-raw` extraction. Row labels for the last two rows are printed after the numbers. The column mapping was checked by arithmetic: 4574-3103 = 1471, 2978-4117 = -1139, 2978/4117 = 72%, 4594-3976 = 618.

resolvedSources.title: Accord de Paris sur le climat – Contribution Déterminée au niveau National, CDN-actualisée Tunisie, Synthèse
resolvedSources.publisher: République Tunisienne, Ministère en charge de l'Environnement
resolvedSources.extracts:
Section 2.1.1 "Ressources en eau", printed page 28. Footnote 17 reads "Scenario RCP 8.5 à l'horizon 2050."

> Les projections climatiques 17 indiquent que les ressources en eau seront particulièrement exposées à : i) l'augmentation de la demande en eau et des conflits d'usages ; ii) la surexploitation des nappes souterraines ; iii) la baisse des stocks d'eau, et iv) la dégradation de la qualité des eaux y compris la salinisation des nappes littorales. Les pertes totales en ressources en eau de ces nappes à l'horizon 2050, ont été évaluées à environ 220 millions de m3 par an, ce qui représente environ 75% de l'ensemble des ressources phréatiques littorales.

English gloss: Under RCP8.5 to 2050, water resources are exposed to rising demand and use conflicts, aquifer overexploitation, falling stocks, and worsening water quality including salinisation of coastal aquifers. Total losses from these coastal aquifers by 2050 are estimated at about 220 Mm3/yr, about 75% of all coastal shallow-aquifer resources.

Section 2.1.4 "Littoral", printed page 28:

> Par ailleurs, sur le domaine littoral tunisien oriental une bonne partie de la ressource hydrique est fournie par les nappes phréatiques côtières qui présentent une forte vulnérabilité face à l'ENM aux conséquences de la salinisation. Ainsi, 44% des côtes tunisiennes sont classées vulnérables à très fortement vulnérables

English gloss: On the eastern coast, much of the water supply comes from coastal shallow aquifers that are highly vulnerable to salinisation from sea-level rise. 44% of Tunisian coasts are classed as vulnerable to very highly vulnerable.

Box, printed page 47:

> Les projections montrent également une baisse des précipitations (-10% à 30% en 2050), l'élévation du niveau de la mer (30 cm à 50 cm en 2050) et la hausse des phénomènes climatiques extrêmes (inondations et sécheresses).

English gloss: Projections also show a 10-30% fall in precipitation by 2050, sea-level rise of 30-50 cm by 2050, and more extreme events (floods and droughts).

Adaptation measures list (water):

> Mesure 7 : Mise en oeuvre du plan d'action de la Stratégie Eau 2050
resolvedSources.notes:
- Opened via: curl+pdftotext; saw: full text of the synthesis. The official UNFCCC copy (https://unfccc.int/sites/default/files/NDC/2022-06/Tunisia%20Update%20NDC-french.pdf) returned an HTML page to curl, so this mirror of the ministry's September 2021 synthesis was used.
- It is a government policy document that summarises underlying studies without method detail. The precipitation range (-10% to -30% by 2050) is much wider and more pessimistic than the AFD (-6 to -9%) and peer-reviewed (Besbes and Chahed) values. The document does not say which study it comes from.
- The coastal-aquifer loss (75%, about 220 Mm3/yr, RCP8.5) differs from the AFD study's "50%" (SRC-TG-504).

resolvedSources.title: Guide de gestion des eaux pluviales en milieu urbain
resolvedSources.publisher: ANME (Agence Nationale pour la Maîtrise de l'Énergie), programme ACTE with Swiss cooperation (SECO); authors K. Bedoui and R. Känzig
resolvedSources.extracts:
Page numbers are the printed footer numbers of the 86-page PDF, as found in the extracted text.

> "des périodes de sècheresse plus longues et des évènements pluvieux extrêmes causant ainsi des inondations dans plusieurs villes." (p. 6, Introduction)

English gloss: longer droughts and extreme rain events cause floods in several cities.

> "les noues, les bassins de rétention, les puits d'infiltration, ou les citernes de collecte des eaux pluviales à partir des toitures. Ces solutions sont souvent moins coûteuses que les techniques traditionnelles, elles nécessitent également moins d'entretien" (p. 6)

English gloss: swales, retention basins, infiltration wells and roof-water cisterns are often cheaper and need less maintenance than traditional (piped) techniques.

> "Sfax compte environ 150'000 Majels" (p. 10, citing A. Bennasr and E. Verdeil)

English gloss: Sfax has about 150,000 majels (underground rainwater cisterns).

> "Les eaux pluviales ne respecte pas forcément ces normes, notamment celles de l'eau potable qui sont très strictes." / "plusieurs régions utilisent les eaux pluviales pour la boisson après un traitement par javellisation qui permet d'améliorer la qualité bactériologique de ces eaux mais n'a aucun effet sur leur qualité physicochimique (notamment sur la présence de métaux lourds, de carbonates, etc.)" / "les propriétaires effectuent rarement des analyses bactériologiques de l'eau." (pp. 17-18)

English gloss: rainwater does not necessarily meet the strict drinking-water standards; chlorination improves bacteriology but not heavy metals; owners rarely test the water.

> "L'article 8 du décret gouvernemental n°2018-171 du 19 février 2018 fixant les conditions d'utilisation des eaux stockées exige que les eaux pluviales collectées des terrasses de bâtiments non accessibles et leurs dépendances peuvent être utilisées dans les usages extérieurs (comme l'irrigation des espaces verts ou le lavage de voitures) et intérieurs du bâtiment (comme les chasses d'eau ou les lave-linge) et doivent être équipées d'un réseau indépendant. En revanche, les eaux pluviales ne peuvent être utilisées comme eau potable, pour la préparation des produits alimentaires ou pour la baignade." (pp. 17-18)

English gloss: Article 8 of Decree 2018-171 allows water from inaccessible building roofs to be used for outdoor uses (green-space irrigation, car washing) and indoor uses (toilets, washing machines) through a separate network, but not for drinking, food preparation or bathing.

> "L'article 9 du même décret exige de chaque utilisateur d'un bâtiment de contrôler de façon périodique les eaux pluviales collectées, en faisant appel au moins une fois par an à un laboratoire spécialisé." (p. 18)

English gloss: Article 9 requires users to have collected rainwater tested by a laboratory at least once a year.

> "Le cadre réglementaire impose l'obligation de mettre en place des bâches de collecte des eaux pluviales pour tout projet de construction conformément aux dispositions du décret n°2018-171 du 19 février 2018" and "Article 3 : Le programme fonctionnel et technique de tout projet de bâtiment civil [...] doit intégrer la composante relative à la réalisation des bâches de collecte des eaux pluviales, sur la base d'une étude de faisabilité [...] approuvée par le ministère de l'agriculture" (p. 19)

English gloss: the regulations oblige every construction project to include a rainwater collection tank, under Decree 2018-171; Article 3 requires a feasibility study approved by the agriculture ministry.

> "le code de l'urbanisme et les plans d'aménagement et de développement urbain représentent l'assise réglementaire pour l'adoption et la dissémination de ces techniques durables." (p. 13)

English gloss: the urban planning code and urban development plans are the regulatory basis for adopting these techniques; the guide presents them as an option, not an obligation.

> "Ce système d'incitation semble insuffisant et ne permet pas de promouvoir la collecte des eaux pluviales en Tunisie." / "le cout d'une citerne enterrée de collecte d'eau pluviale d'une capacité de 20m3 en maçonnerie coute entre 13'000 DNT et 15'000 DNT. Si on opte pour des citernes en plastique le coût sera réduit à moins de 4'000 DNT. Cependant, le projet reste économiquement non rentable en raison des faibles tarifs de l'eau" (p. 15)

English gloss: the loan incentive looks insufficient; a 20 m3 buried masonry cistern costs 13,000-15,000 TND, a plastic one under 4,000 TND, but it is still not profitable because water tariffs are low. (The guide's text says "20 m2" in one place and "20m3" in another; the capacity is read as 20 m3.)

> "il est recommandé qu'un événement pluvieux de 5 à 15 mm par mètre carré de terrain soit stocké, évaporé ou infiltré sur le même terrain." (p. 36)

English gloss: as an order of magnitude, a rain event of 5 to 15 mm per square metre should be stored, evaporated or infiltrated on the same plot.

> "Le stockage de l'eau n'a de sens que si celle-ci est ensuite utilisée pour d'autres usages, comme la végétalisation des toits ou les toilettes." (p. 36)

English gloss: storage only makes sense if the water is then used for other purposes.

> "Prescrire l'infiltration de l'eau propre sur tous les terrains." (p. 39, measure for the urban development plan)

English gloss: prescribe infiltration of clean water on all plots (a recommendation to municipalities).
resolvedSources.notes: A Tunisian national-agency guide for municipalities, written with Swiss support and drawing on European (German and Swiss) "sponge city" practice. It is a guide, not a law. Its descriptions of decrees (2018-171, 2016-1125) are paraphrases: the decree texts were not opened. It does not mention ACO or geocellular tanks. The figures on costs are undated and not sourced inside the guide.

resolvedSources.title: Impact of runoff infiltration on contaminant accumulation and transport in the soil/filter media of Sustainable Urban Drainage Systems: A literature review
resolvedSources.publisher: Science of The Total Environment, vol. 569-570, pp. 904-926 (Tedoldi, Chebbo, Pierlot, Kovacs, Gromaire)
resolvedSources.extracts:
Abstract, read through the Europe PMC record (PMID 27432725); the full text was not opened.

> "The increasing use of Sustainable Urban Drainage Systems (SUDS) for stormwater management raises some concerns about the fate of ubiquitous runoff micropollutants in soils and their potential threat to groundwater."

> "most investigations undoubtedly evidenced a significant accumulation of metals and/or hydrocarbons in SUDS soils, which in the majority of the cases appears to be restricted to the upper 10 to 30cm. These results may suggest that SUDS exhibit an interesting potential for pollution control, but antinomic observations have also been made in several specific cases, and the inter-site concentration variability is still difficult to appraise."

English gloss: infiltration systems accumulate metals and hydrocarbons, mostly in the top 10-30 cm of soil. This suggests good pollution control, but contrary cases exist and site-to-site variability is hard to predict.
resolvedSources.notes: A review of mostly European and North American studies in temperate climates; no Tunisian or arid-climate case. It concerns soil-based devices (swales, basins, filter media). It does not assess buried plastic tanks that discharge directly into the soil below the surface layer, where the surface soil does not filter the water first; that is an inference in SOL-TG-400, not a finding of this review.
